clue.text: Approve of transfer temporarily

explanation.surface: Someone backs a plan to move staff for a short spell.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a motion is to support it formally; to second an employee is to lend them to another post for a time.

clue.text: A-m-e-r-i-c-a-n p-r-o-d-c-e-r n-a-m-e-d A-a-ro-n

parts.note: the words name the Hollywood TV producer Aaron with that surname, and the hyphens show the clue itself being written out letter by letter

explanation.walkthrough: Aaron Spelling produced American TV shows such as Dynasty; the joke is that the clue is printed letter by letter. The held text has lost a U and a hyphen in the OCR, which does not affect the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing words out letter by letter is the act of orthography, and the surname of the producer of Dynasty is the same word.

clue.text: Take medicine, perhaps, swallowing a pint

indicators.note: the remedy takes the other pieces into its middle, as if gulping them down

parts.note: medicine is one kind of cure or remedy

explanation.surface: Instructions to down a dose of medicine with a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To capture something is to seize or take hold of it.

clue.text: Einstein's decade?

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: the letters of the word for the 90s, rearranged in a mischievous way, spell this physicist's surname

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: taking the answer's second word and treating its first word as a signal to scramble produces EINSTEIN. The 1890s were the Naughty Nineties in Britain, the era of Oscar Wilde.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1890s are known in Britain by this nickname for their supposed decadence, so it names a ten-year period.

clue.text: Promoted a recording about an English church

indicators.note: the disc goes around the other letters, surrounding them

parts.note: a DVD is a recording on disc
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone got promoted after releasing a recording about an English church.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone advanced has been moved up or furthered in rank, like a promotion.

clue.text: Exercise for dimwit

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Exercise for dimwit (4)' lacks the word giving DO; the blog parses DOPE as DO + PE, so a word such as 'Do' or 'Party' is missing from the OCR text.

clue.text: Insurance company employee given claim a judge rates incorrect

parts.note: to aver is to claim or assert

indicators.note: the words are wrong as they stand and must be put into a different order

explanation.surface: An insurance clerk handling a claim judged wrongly by a magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrect' rearranges A JUDGE RATES into AGE ADJUSTER after AVER. 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An average adjuster is a specialist who assesses marine insurance losses for insurers.

clue.text: Russian revolutionary repeatedly wanting end to rebellion

indicators.note: the revolutionary's name is written twice over, one copy after another

parts.note: Che Guevara is the stock crossword revolutionary

indicators.note: end to means only the final letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A revolutionary in Russia keeps hoping the rebellion will end.
explanation.definitionFit: Chechnya is a republic within the Russian Federation, so a native of it is a citizen of that country.

clue.text: Imprisoned by bandit, heroes show agitation

indicators.note: the answer sits locked up within the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Heroes held captive by a bandit get nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to be flustered and indecisive, a visible sign of nerves.

clue.text: Explain old avoirdupois unit

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
the pound is a unit of weight in the avoirdupois system

explanation.surface: A request to have an old unit of weight explained.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to set out and interpret something in detail.

clue.text: Agreed troublesome sons can enter gymkhana event

indicators.note: the two letters for sons are able to go into the middle of the jumbled word
being troublesome, the letters of the word refuse to stay in order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, so SS is sons

explanation.surface: It was agreed that unruly boys could take part in the pony show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troublesome' looks like it describes the sons, but it scrambles the first word, and 'can enter' is the insertion signal. A gymkhana is a horse-riding competition, often for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is a competitive discipline of trained horse movements, one of the events at a riding show.

clue.text: Comedy award subsequently attracts expression of disapproval

parts.note: to award is to present, give formally

indicators.note: the word for later pulls the exclamation into its middle

parts.note: subsequently means later
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A comedy wins a prize but later draws boos.
explanation.walkthrough: Present Laughter is a 1939 comedy play by Noël Coward.
explanation.definitionFit: This Noël Coward play is a comic stage work, so it is an example of a comedy.

clue.text: See 11
Brew that is served in old-fashioned club

parts.note: mash is the malt and water mixture brewed into beer
ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Beer is served in a traditional gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' is a golf club, not a social one; 'served in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mashie was a golf iron of the pre-numbered era, roughly a modern five iron.

clue.text: Cultured society girl taking part in radio show

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering high society
being broadcast live is being on air

explanation.surface: A refined debutante appears on a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave and sophisticated, polished in manner.

clue.text: Poor journalist must get in some money after retiring

indicators.note: the editor goes inside the currency once it has been turned round
retiring means drawing back, so the currency is read from right to left

parts.note: the yen is Japan's currency
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A broke reporter needs cash coming in after he stops work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after retiring' turns the currency backwards to NEY before the journalist goes in; 'must' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy means lacking money and essentials, so it is a synonym of poor.

clue.text: Irish drinking places providing novel snack, say

parts.note: She is a famous novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the snack only sounds like the letters needed

parts.note: beans on toast is a classic British snack

explanation.surface: Pubs in Ireland serving a new kind of bar snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel snack' tempts an anagram; 'novel' is the book SHE. 'say' gives BEENS, which sounds like BEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed Irish bar, a place for illicit drinking.

clue.text: Month after month Yard's seized ecstasy and cannabis

indicators.note: the two months take hold of the letter for yard between them
the first month named is placed after the second one

parts.note: Mar is the abbreviation for March
Jan is the abbreviation for January
Y is the abbreviation for yard
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Every month Scotland Yard makes another seizure of ecstasy and cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as police seizing drugs, but 'seized' is the container signal and 'after' orders the months. Scotland Yard is London's police headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Jane is an old slang name for marijuana.

clue.text: Beginning to like carpeting with length cut

indicators.note: cut means a letter is chopped out of the longer word

parts.note: carpeting is British slang for a telling-off, a stern lecture

explanation.surface: Starting to enjoy having new carpet fitted, cut to size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpeting' is not floor covering but a reprimand; 'cut' removes L for length.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking to someone means starting to feel fond of them.

clue.text: In a tizzy, take one?

indicators.note: In at the front tells us the next pieces go inside the state of agitation

parts.note: to be in a tizzy is to be in a spin
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Advice to someone flustered: swallow a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts R and I inside A SPIN. R for 'take' comes from the Rx symbol on prescriptions. The whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirin is a common painkiller tablet, the pill a frazzled person might swallow.

clue.text: I have semi-detached property abroad

parts.note: the setter is Dac, so I in his clue is DAC

indicators.note: semi-detached here means only half of the following word is kept, its front portion

explanation.surface: Someone owns a semi-detached house overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often use 'I' for their own pseudonym. A semi-detached is a British house sharing one wall with its neighbour; here it means 'half'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house, a holiday home in a foreign land.

clue.text: Fish cooker?

explanation.definitionFit: A codling is a young cod, a sea creature; it is also a variety of apple used for cooking rather than eating raw.

clue.text: China's overwhelmed Pacific region first

indicators.note: the friend engulfs the region, closing around it

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate, so pal
the Pacific Rim is the region around that ocean

explanation.surface: China is said to have dominated the Pacific before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate), not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means original or earliest, the very first in time.

clue.text: Kanye West possibly making cover version for listeners

indicators.note: a version for listeners is one heard by ear rather than seen on paper

parts.note: a wrapper is a cover or casing

explanation.surface: A hip-hop star records a cover version for his fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover version' looks musical; 'cover' is WRAPPER, which sounds like the answer because the W is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Kanye West is a famous hip-hop artist, an example of someone who performs rap.

clue.text: Many a store not closing during busy part of weekend

indicators.note: busy suggests the letters are bustling about and so reshuffled
not closing means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Lots of shops stay open through the hectic weekend rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not closing' trims STORE to STOR; 'busy' mixes MANY A, STOR and DURING together.
explanation.definitionFit: The first half of the day after Friday is a portion of the weekend.

clue.text: Monster conger eel appears intermittently

indicators.note: intermittently means taking letters at intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: A huge conger eel surfaces now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, a frightening creature.

clue.text: See 24
Tries an unusual wine

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are arranged in a strange new way

explanation.surface: Someone sampling an odd wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Country prophet and painter

parts.note: a land is a country
a seer is one who foresees, a prophet

explanation.surface: A list of a nation, a soothsayer and an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter of animals who designed the lions in Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin Landseer was a celebrated English artist.

clue.text: Gear up for a spin in European capital

indicators.note: taking letters for a spin means whirling them into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting the car ready for a drive into a Continental city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear up' looks like 'reverse GEAR', but 'for a spin' rearranges both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Prague is the capital city of the Czech Republic.
